chunk_findings.detail: `wt = Path(out.data["worktree"])` treats the worktree path as absolute or relative to the current process cwd, not relative to `repo`. The incident itself shows worktrees are represented as repo-relative paths like `.ddflow/worktrees/B95-false-limit`. When pytest runs with cwd != `repo` (the normal `tmp_path` fixture case), `(wt / rel)` and `_git("-C", str(wt), ...)` target a directory under the wrong repository, so `_git` raises `CalledProcessError: not a git repository` before either test reaches its assertions. The path should be `Path(repo) / out.data["worktree"]`.

chunk_findings.detail: `wt = Path(out.data["worktree"])` resolves `LC.claim`'s worktree path against the pytest process current directory, not against the temporary `repo`. The claimed worktree path is repo-relative (the same `.ddflow/worktrees/<item>` form quoted in the bug report and expected by the recovery assertions), so when pytest runs from the checkout, `_git("-C", str(wt), "add", "-A")` operates on `<checkout>/.ddflow/worktrees/T1` rather than `repo/.ddflow/worktrees/T1`. That directory is not a git repository, so `git` raises `CalledProcessError`, making both new tests error before they exercise the fix. The helper must join the path to the repo, e.g. `wt = repo / out.data["worktree"]`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change fixes bug B-recover-forgets-author-model, but the manifest lists only `ddflow/api/lifecycle/author.py`, `ddflow/api/lifecycle/complete/finish.py`, `ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py`, and a new test file. It includes no task record naming the phase this work counts toward, its dependencies in `needs`, and its `wave:N` tag. Since the rule says it covers bug fix tasks filed by ddflow, the missing task metadata violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave].
chunk_findings.title: MANIFEST [r-task-phase-needs-wave]

chunk_findings.detail: In `_merged`, the seeded `task.added` event defines task `T1` with `{"parent": "P1", "title": item, "globs": [rel]}` but omits the `needs` field and the required `wave:N`/`no-deps` tag. [r-task-phase-needs-wave] says every task must state dependencies in `needs` and carry a wave tag; a task with no prerequisite must carry `no-deps`. Since `T1` has no prerequisite and no wave tag, the fixture creates a non-compliant ddflow task, so these regression tests seed invalid state under the project rule.

evidence.note: Claim: complete --model is used only in-memory and a refusal records it nowhere, so recover/lanes report 'the author's model is unknown'; recover also names a worktree merge removed. Probe: tests/test_recover_forgets_author_model.py. Verdict CONFIRMED: on unfixed code test_a_refused_complete_with_model_remembers_the_author_model fails open_session_model='' != claude-opus-5-5 and test_recover_omits_a_worktree_a_merge_removed fails rec.worktree='.ddflow/worktrees/T1' != ''; both pass after the fix.

Read the applicable rules surfaced at claim: r-task-phase-needs-wave (fix task already carries parent bugs-2 + wave:0), r-gemini-key-load (gemini key exported before review), r-alert-owner-next-call, r-bounded-everything. Fix follows the recorded model-provenance decision (model recorded on session.started, never guessed).

author.py: _remember_declared_model records a --model flag as a session declaration (deduped) so recover/lanes read it past a refusal; finish.py calls it after _author_model; leases/recovery.py clears rec.worktree when the tree is gone.

roborev job 4245 (sha 83f5c54) found 2 findings: [medium] _remember_declared_model opened a fresh never-ended session masking the lanes 'ended' signal -> FIXED by merging the model into the agent's existing session (sessions.start session_id=current.id); [low] no lanes regression -> ADDED test_a_refused_complete_merges_the_model_into_the_existing_session. Re-review job 4251 (sha 891ec9e) confirms both addressed; residual low (a session.started merge event on an already-ended id) is this codebase's documented 'Merge, never replace' fold idiom (importer/prompt-hook re-append session.started to fixed ids); model read stays correct.
